tools.name: intel_cyclones
tools.description: Get active tropical cyclones from the US National Hurricane Center: name, classification, intensity (knots), pressure (mb), position, movement, by-basin grouping. Covers the Atlantic, Eastern and Central Pacific basins only - Western Pacific / Indian Ocean storms (JTWC) are not included. Zero storms means a quiet tropics, not an outage; a fetch failure carries an explicit error. No API key needed. Optional: include_forecast (default false) adds each storm's official forecast track from its NHC forecast/advisory (positions with UTC valid times and forecast hours, max wind and gusts in knots, post-tropical/dissipated status) and the 5-day cone of uncertainty as [lat, lon] vertices simplified to 0.01 degrees (NHC's KMZ linked); a track or cone that could not be fetched is named in data_gaps and marks the response degraded.

include_forecast.description: Add each storm's forecast track and cone (one text and one KMZ fetch per storm, at most 10 storms per call). Default false.

Covers Europe only - 39 participating countries, each with its own feed (no Europe-wide feed exists); call without country to list available countries. Awareness color is derived from the warning title. Zero alerts means calm weather, not an outage; a fetch failure carries an explicit error. Content CC BY 4.0-equivalent. No API key needed.

country.description: Country name or slug (e.g. france, united-kingdom, uk). Omit to get the available-country roster.

limit.description: Max alerts (default 50); one warning may span several area entries

tools.name: intel_jtwc_cyclones
tools.description: Get active tropical cyclone warnings from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center: storm id, name, classification, warning number, issue time, warning text/graphic links, by-basin grouping, plus significant tropical weather advisories. Covers the Northwest Pacific, North Indian Ocean, and Southern Hemisphere; its Central/Eastern Pacific item overlaps NHC (intel_cyclones). Positions and intensities are not in the feed - they live in the linked warning products. Zero storms means quiet basins, not an outage. No API key needed. Optional: include_forecast (default false) fetches each storm's warning text and adds its warning position, intensity and pressure plus the forecast track (positions with UTC valid times, forecast hours, max sustained winds and gusts in knots, status lines such as EXTRATROPICAL); JTWC publishes no cone of uncertainty, so cone is null. A warning text that could not be fetched is named in data_gaps and marks the response degraded.

include_forecast.description: Add each storm's forecast track from its warning text (one fetch per storm, at most 10 storms per call). Default false.

tools.name: intel_jet_activity_anomaly
tools.description: Early-warning check: peak concurrent airborne cohort aircraft (business jets or military) in the latest published UTC half-hour (or a given slot) vs the same slot on prior same-weekday dates, from adsb.lol globe_history heatmaps. US federal holiday-adjacent baseline dates are swapped for earlier weeks. Returns robust z-score, alert level 1-5 (normal/watch/elevated/high/alarm), deficit flag, and data gaps. Needs a learned cohort (see intel_jet_cohort_snapshot); downloads ~14 MB per uncached slot, cached on disk.

region.description: global, conus, north_america, europe, middle_east, east_asia, or 'lamin,lomin,lamax,lomax'

slot.description: UTC ISO datetime inside the half-hour to score (default: latest published)

min_learning_lead_hours.description: Only use cohort members first seen this long before the window (avoids selection bias). Negative values admit later-learned members for a first look; the result is then marked degraded with a selection-bias data gap.

upstream.handlerSource:

        slot=arguments.get("slot"),
        alarm_sigma=float(arguments.get("alarm_sigma", 5.0)),

tools.name: intel_jet_excess_origins

Infers takeoffs and landings from adsb.lol heatmap tracks for a 0.5-2 h window and the same window on prior weeks, density-clusters the endpoints (default 12-mile radius), and reports clusters above their baseline median with a pattern label: departure_anchor, arrival_anchor, regional concentration, diffuse, or no_excess. Optional reference point gives distance-to-event. At most 12 heatmap files (~14 MB each, cached) per call.

start.description: UTC ISO start of the window (default: ends at the latest published slot)

ref_lat.description: Optional event latitude for distance reporting

ref_lon.description: Optional event longitude for distance reporting

min_learning_lead_hours.description: Only use cohort members first seen this long before the window; negative admits later-learned members (marked as a selection-bias data gap)

tools.name: intel_lagged_connections
tools.description: Correlation between 2 to 8 series in the history store (keys as intel_series_history lists them), aligned on a UTC day, week or month grid and tested at every lag from -max_lag to +max_lag. Default transform is period-over-period changes, because levels of trending series correlate spuriously; 'levels' on request. Per pair: the lag with the strongest evidence (smallest p) with Pearson r, overlap n, two-sided p from Student's t treating periods as independent, p_ar1 recomputed with an AR(1) effective sample size from both series' lag-1 autocorrelations, and the Benjamini-Hochberg q and q_ar1 across every test in the call. Significant means q_ar1 <= 0.05 by default (significant_if_independent applies it to q); serial_correlation_dominates and data_gaps name autocorrelated series, and an effective sample below 3 is reported as no evidence. Lag +k compares A at period t with B at t+k, so A leads B by k. Pair/lag overlaps under 30 points are listed as not tested. Revised points use the latest vintage; rows without observed_at (Yahoo quotes) are not used. States what it cannot prove: correlation is not causation and a lead is not a causal direction. History accrues only while the collector (intel-collector, or intel_collect) runs; nothing before its first recorded cycle exists.

series_keys.description: 2 to 8 series keys, e.g. ['space_weather:kp', 'central_bank_rates:federal_funds_rate']; pairs are formed in this order

grid.description: UTC calendar grid (default day; weeks run Monday to Sunday)

max_lag.description: Largest lead or lag in grid periods (default 5, clamped to 0..30, reduced to keep a call within 1000 tests)

min_overlap.description: Fewest overlapping periods a pair/lag needs to be tested (default 30, clamped to 20..3000)

q.description: False discovery rate threshold applied to q_ar1 (default 0.05, clamped to 0.001..0.25)

start.description: First date YYYY-MM-DD; its grid period and later are used (moved later, and reported, when the window would exceed 3000 periods)

end.description: Last date YYYY-MM-DD; its grid period and earlier are used

upstream.handlerSource:
async def _lagged_connections(arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    # Up to 1,000 tests over up to 3,000 periods is CPU-bound for a moment,
    # so it runs off the event loop. The path is resolved here, on the loop
    # thread: a first touch of runtime.cache opens the shared Cache, whose
    # sqlite connection must not be born in a worker thread.
    db_path = runtime.cache.db_path
    return await asyncio.to_thread(_run, db_path, arguments)

Items carry observed_at, published_at and collected_at where known. Says which records are past retention (payload bodies 7 days, run log 30, observations 365 by default) or before the run log starts, instead of reading them as a quiet day. Output is capped (in by=observed both lists share the caps) and truncation is stated. Read-only: never fetches. History accrues only while the collector (intel-collector, or intel_collect) runs.

tools.name: intel_history_backfill
tools.description: Load the history FRED (graph CSV) or the ECB Data Portal already serve into the history store, for intel_series_history and intel_revisions: one capture per request (a FRED id, or an ECB key that may match several series) under backfill:fred or backfill:ecb, observed_at from the publisher's dates, published_at null (neither names a release date), collected_at the backfill time. Values are the publisher's current vintage, so revisions made before the first backfill are invisible; a re-run stores only new or changed values, and a changed value is a revision. FRED missing values are skipped and counted; ECB missing values cannot be counted (null). A failed fetch, or one answered only from a stale cache copy, is an error capture and stores no values. This tool writes to the history store and sends requests upstream, so it is capped: at most 5 FRED series or 2 ECB keys (20 series each) per call, the newest 20000 points per series and 100000 per call. A repeat within the cache window (FRED 1 h, ECB 3 h) reads the cached response and sends no request.

series.description: FRED series ids (e.g. ['WALCL', 'RRPONTSYD']) or ECB series keys DATASET.KEY (e.g. ['BSI.M.U2.Y.V.M30.X.1.U2.2300.Z01.E'])

It needs UCDP_ACCESS_TOKEN: without it, or when the API refuses it, the tool returns an error with reason ucdp_unconfigured or ucdp_fetch_failed, which is missing data, not zero events. It has no country filter, so keep the events in {country} yourself, split them at {days} days ago by date_start, and say that you filtered. limit is the page size and every page is requested, so it does not cap the result. When a page could not be fetched the result carries reason ucdp_partial and pages_failed: its count and fatalities are then lower bounds, so say the list is incomplete

ACLED events in {country} over both windows. It needs ACLED_EMAIL and ACLED_PASSWORD; without them it returns an error naming them. limit caps the result: a count equal to the limit means the list may have been cut off, so say so or call again with a higher limit

limits: Event datasets are revised and arrive late, so the most recent days are the least complete. A quiet final week is not proof of calm.

UCDP is read from one pinned GED release (gedevents/25.1), which holds events only up to its own cutoff. The tool states neither that cutoff nor a marker when your window lies after it: it drops the older events and returns count 0. Check the latest date_start UCDP returned; when count is 0, or the newest event is well before the window ends, UCDP has no data for that span, which is missing data, not zero events.
Count events and fatalities separately: fewer events with more deaths is not de-escalation.
